title: Alan Turing
summary: Alan Mathison Turing OBE FRS (23 June 1912 – 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist. Turing was highly influential in the development of theoretical computer science, providing a formalisation of the concepts of algorithm and computation with the Turing machine, which can be considered a model of a general-purpose computer. He is widely considered to be the father of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence.

quiz.question: Where did Alan Turing study as an undergraduate?
quiz.explanation: Turing studied at King's College, Cambridge, as mentioned in the 'Early life and education' section.

quiz.question: What was Alan Turing's main contribution during World War II?
quiz.explanation: Turing worked at Bletchley Park where he played a crucial role in breaking German ciphers, particularly the Enigma machine, as detailed in the 'Cryptanalysis' section.

quiz.question: What theoretical concept did Turing introduce that became fundamental to computer science?
quiz.explanation: The Turing Machine, introduced in his 1936 paper, provided a formalization of the concepts of algorithm and computation and is considered a model of a general-purpose computer.

quiz.question: In what year did Alan Turing die?
quiz.explanation: Alan Turing died on 7 June 1954, as stated in the article's opening paragraph.

quiz.question: What test did Turing propose to determine if a machine can exhibit intelligent behavior?
quiz.explanation: Turing proposed the Turing Test (originally called the 'imitation game') as a criterion of intelligence in machines.

quiz.question: What honor was Turing awarded in 1945 for his wartime services?
quiz.explanation: Turing was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE) in 1945 for his work during World War II.

quiz.question: What field did Turing work on towards the end of his life involving patterns in nature?
quiz.explanation: Turing turned to mathematical biology and worked on morphogenesis - the pattern formation in biological organisms, as mentioned in the article.
